newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt drifts lower amid new issues vigil.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt drifts lower amid new issues vigil.

text.p: Emerging debt prices slipped slightly on Monday as players treaded water in the hope that bond issuance by Russia and Brazil would revive a somnolent Brady market, traders said.
"You have had a lull of activity in the secondary market, but there is a lot of activity in the new issue market," said one emerging market researcher at one U.S. bank.
Dealers found scarce news to influence Brady bond prices, as Latin paper slipped across the board, while Russian and Eastern European debt ended stronger.

Absent fundamental news and with only second-tier U.S. economic data due this week, players focused on Russia's inaugural Eurobond, likely to be launched by November, and the roadshow later this week for a Brazil $750 million bond.
"The market reception to both of those issues will probably provide the next indication of where the market is going," said Joyce Chang, managing director at Merrill Lynch.
Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR slipped 1/4 to 82-1/8, while Brazilian C bonds BR8D14=RR slipped 7/8 to 70-3/4 and Mexico's global bond due 2026 MXUMS=RR closed unchanged dipped 1/4 to 99-1/2.

One Brady trader who specializes in Brazil debt at a large U.S. bank said that some players seemed to get out of their C bond positions out of concern for potential volatility in the U.S. stock market.
"I saw a little sellng from investors," the trader said. "People are looking at the Dow."

Brazil paper got hit by a suprising amount of short selling, given the overall thin conditions of the market, one dealer said. Russian dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR ended 7/8 higher to 77-5/8, although most of the gains occurred in early trade. -- George Lerner, 212-859-1671
